messages.quote: This excludes from this halakha items that are consecrated for Temple maintenance

notes.he: דהא ברייתא סייעתא להו מי אמרת כו':
notes.en: Rav Beivai would tell you: “And from it” [Rabbeinu Gershom reads umina, “and from it,” where the printed Gemara reads bar mina, “apart from it”]: for the baraita itself supports him: didn’t you say, and so on.

messages.text: Here too, just as the case of one’s sister is unique in that she is a forbidden relative who cannot be permitted during the entire life of the one who prohibits her, i.e., her brother, as she will always be his sister, so too, the halakha that one is liable to bring a sin offering for the transgression of each prohibition applies to any forbidden relative who cannot be permitted in the life of the one who prohibits her.

notes.dh: אשת איש שיש לה היתר בחיי אוסרה
notes.he: שמתגרשת בגט הלכך לא גמרי לה מאחותו ולא משכחת בה בחטאת בהעלם:
notes.en: A married woman, who can be permitted in the life of the one who prohibits her: since she can be divorced with a bill of divorce. Therefore she is not derived from his sister, and a sin offering [for each one] within a single lapse is not found with her.

notes.dh: שאין לה היתר בחיי אוסרה יצתה אשת איש
notes.he: הוי מצי למימר מה אחותו שאין לה היתר כלל אף כל כו' יצאת אשת אח שיש לה היתר במקום מצוה:
notes.en: Who cannot be permitted in the life of the one who prohibits her; a married woman is excluded: he could also have said: just as his sister can never be permitted at all, so too every [relation that can never be permitted], which excludes a brother’s wife, who is permitted where there is a mitzva [of levirate marriage].

notes.dh: הכא נמי מה אחותו מיוחדת שהיא ערוה ואין לה היתר לעולם בחיי אוסרה
notes.he: שאינה מותרת לעולם לאחיו שאוסרה אף כל שאין לה היתר בחיי אוסרה חייבין עליה כרת:
notes.en: Here too: just as his sister is distinct in that she is a forbidden relation who can never be permitted in the life of the one who prohibits her, since she is never permitted to her brother who prohibits her, so too for every [relation] who cannot be permitted in the life of the one who prohibits her, one is liable to karet.

messages.text: This excludes a married woman, who can be permitted in the life of the one who prohibits her, i.e., her husband, as their relationship can be terminated by means of divorce. If so, one would not be liable to bring a separate sin offering for each instance of engaging in intercourse with a married woman, whereas Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains that one is liable to bring a sin offering for violating each of the prohibitions listed in the mishna, including the one concerning a married woman.

notes.he: יצאת אשת איש שיש לה היתר בחיי אוסרה שאם נתן לה גט מותרת וכן נדה יש לה היתר לבעלה לאחר נדתה הלכך לא מצי אחותו ללמד על הכלל כולו:
notes.en: Excluding a married woman, who can be permitted in the life of the one who prohibits her, since if he gave her a bill of divorce she is permitted; and likewise a menstruating woman is permitted to her husband after her menstruation. Therefore his sister cannot teach about the entire generalization.

messages.alt: and some say Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua
messages.text: The verse states: “For whoever shall do any of these abominations, the souls that do them shall be cut off from among their people” (Leviticus 18:29).

notes.he: מהכא ילפת לחלק דאמר קרא כי כל אשר יעשה מכל התועבות וגו' וכולהו עריות בין אחותו בין אשת איש בין נדה כולהו שייכי בהאי קרא הואיל וכך דאחותו שייכא בהאי קרא ויצאת ש"מ להיקש הוא ואין משיבין על ההיקש אלא מה זו שיצאת חייבין עליה בפני עצמה אף כל השאר נמי אף אותן שיש בהן היתר בחיי אוסרן:
notes.en: Rabbi Yona said, and so on: from here you derive [the rule] to separate, for the verse states: “For whoever shall do any of these abominations …” (Leviticus 18:29), and all the forbidden relations, whether his sister, a married woman or a menstruating woman, belong to this verse. Since that is so, since his sister belongs to this verse and was singled out, conclude from it that this is a juxtaposition, and one does not refute a juxtaposition. Rather, just as for this one that was singled out one is liable for her by herself, so too for all the others, even those who can be permitted in the life of the one who prohibits them.

messages.alt: and some say Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua
messages.text: Since this is a juxtaposition, it means that in this verse all of those with whom relations are forbidden are juxtaposed to the case of one’s sister, written in that passage, as follows: Just as with regard to one’s sister he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for engaging in intercourse with her alone, so too, with regard to any one of all the cases of forbidden relations, one is liable to bring a separate sin offering for engaging in intercourse with that woman alone. When a halakha is derived by juxtaposition the cases do not have to be entirely similar.

notes.he: אפי' עשאה עם האחרים:
notes.en: By herself: even if he committed it together with the others.

notes.dh: הוקשו כל עריות כולן לאחותו דכתיב ביה כרת
notes.he: וליכא לאקשויי לשתוק מהיקשא ולכתוב כרת באשת איש דקיל או באשת אח וכ"ש שאר עריות די"ל דהיקשא זו איצטריך למילי טובא ביבמות ועוד דמה להנהו שכן בידו לרבות:
notes.en: All the forbidden relations are juxtaposed to his sister, of whom karet is written: one cannot ask: let the verse omit the juxtaposition and write karet with a married woman, which is lenient, or with a brother’s wife, and all the more so would it apply to the other relations. For one can answer that this juxtaposition is needed for many matters in Yevamot. Furthermore, [a derivation from them could be refuted]: what of those, which have the feature that it is in his power to increase [them]?

messages.text: All those liable to receive karet in cases of incest were included in the principle: “For whoever shall commit any of these abominations, even the people who commit them shall be cut off from among their people” (Leviticus 18:29). And why was karet incurred by engaging in intercourse with one’s sister singled out in Leviticus 20:17? It was singled out to judge it, so that the transgressors receive the punishment of karet and not the punishment of lashes. Although they have violated a prohibition, which generally carries the punishment of lashes, they are not flogged, as they are liable to receive the more severe punishment of karet.
messages.lead: The Gemara objects: But this presents a difficulty according to the opinion of Rabbi Yitzḥak, who says:

notes.he: והיה מלמד על הכלל כולו דלית ליה חייבי כריתות שלקו נפטרו מידי כריתתן באלו הן הלוקין (מכות כג.):
notes.en: To judge it with karet and not with lashes: and it would teach about the entire generalization; for he does not hold [the mishna’s principle] that those liable to karet who were flogged are exempt from their karet, in the chapter “These Are the Ones Who Are Flogged” (Makkot 23a).

notes.he: תימה דבשלמים נמי נימא דיצאו לדונו בכרת ולא במלקות:
notes.en: To judge it with karet and not with lashes: this is puzzling, for with peace offerings too, let us say they were singled out to judge it with karet and not with lashes.

notes.he: דפליג במס' מכות עלה דההיא דתנן כל חייבי כריתות שלקו נפטרין מידי כריתתן וקא מפיק להאי למה יצאת כרת באחותו לדונן בכרת ולא במלקות א"כ לחלק לחייב על כל אחת מנא ליה:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Yitzḥak, who disagrees in tractate Makkot with what we learned there, “All those liable to karet who were flogged are exempt from their karet,” and who takes (a printer’s gloss: read “takes this”) the karet written with his sister, which was singled out to judge them, and so on: why was karet singled out with his sister? To judge them with karet and not with lashes. If so, from where does he derive [the rule] to separate, to make him liable for each one?

messages.text: From where does Rabbi Yitzḥak learn to separate the prohibitions and teach that one is liable to receive a separate punishment of karet or to bring a sin offering for each violation of the prohibition against forbidden intercourse? Unlike Rabbi Yoḥanan, he cannot derive it from the above verse, as he learns this aforementioned halakha from that verse.

He derives it from the verse: “And you shall not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness as long as she is impure by her menstruation” (Leviticus 18:19). Since the verse could have stated simply: And you shall not approach a menstruating woman, the lengthy expression of: “A woman…as long as she is impure by her menstruation,” serves to separate the transgressions and render him liable to receive a punishment for each and every woman with whom he engaged in forbidden sexual intercourse.

verse.he: וְאֶל־אִשָּׁה בְּנִדַּת טֻמְאָתָהּ לֹא תִקְרַב לְגַלּוֹת עֶרְוָתָהּ׃
verse.en: Do not come near a woman during her menstrual period of impurity to uncover her nakedness.

notes.he: הוה ליה למיכתב ולנדה לא תקרב:
notes.en: “And to a woman”: it should have written, “And to a menstruating woman you shall not approach.”

notes.he: מואל אשה בנדת טומאתה דמצי למימר ואל נדה בטומאתה אמאי קאמר ואל אשה ש"מ לחלק על כל אשה ואשה של עריות דהאי ואל אשה סמוך לפרשה דעריות:
notes.en: He derives it from “And to a woman in the impurity of her menstruation”: since it could have said, “And to a menstruating woman in her impurity,” why does it say “And to a woman”? Conclude from it: to separate for each and every woman among the forbidden relations, since this “And to a woman” is adjacent to the passage of the forbidden relations.

messages.text: And with regard to the Rabbis, who disagree with Rabbi Yitzḥak, let them also derive this halakha that one is liable to receive a separate punishment of karet or to bring a sin offering for each violation of the prohibition against forbidden intercourse from the verse cited by Rabbi Yitzḥak: “And you shall not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness as long as she is impure by her menstruation.”

notes.he: דאית להו נפטרו מידי כריתתן ומפקי כרת דאחותו לחלק:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: who hold that [those liable to karet who were flogged] are exempt from their karet, and who take the karet stated with his sister to separate.

notes.he: לחלק:
notes.en: Let them derive it from “And to a woman”: to separate.

messages.text: Yes, it is indeed so.
But if they derive that halakha from the same source as Rabbi Yitzḥak, for what purpose does the specific instance of karet stated with regard to one’s sister come?

The Rabbis require it to separate the transgressions and render one liable to bring a separate sin offering for engaging in intercourse with his sister, and for engaging in intercourse with his father’s sister, and for engaging in intercourse with his mother’s sister, in a single lapse of awareness.

notes.dh: על אחותו ועל אחות אביו ועל אחות אמו
notes.he: דסד"א הואיל ואיסור חד דאחוה אכולהו לא נחייב אלא חדא:
notes.en: For his sister, and for his father’s sister, and for his mother’s sister: for it might have entered your mind that since a single prohibition, that of sisterhood, applies to all of them, he is liable only once.

notes.he: מיתבעי להון לחלק לחייב בין על אחותו בין על אחות אביו בין על אחות אמו:
notes.en: They need it to separate, to make him liable for his sister, for his father’s sister and for his mother’s sister.

messages.text: Why is it necessary for the verse to separate the transgressions and render one liable to bring a separate sin offering with regard to these forbidden relatives? Aren’t they separate categories of prohibitions, and aren’t they separate bodies, i.e., three different people? It is obvious that each act of intercourse will require a separate sin offering.

notes.he: מואל אשה נפקא מקראות מוחלקין דמתלתא קראי נפקי אחותו ואחות אביו ואחות אמו:
notes.en: Aren’t they separate names: this is already derived from “And to a woman.” They are separate verses, since his sister, his father’s sister and his mother’s sister are derived from three verses.

notes.he: הני למה להון לחלק פשיטא דחייב על כל אחת בפ"ע דהרי שמות מוחלקין דזו קרויה אחותו וזו אחות אביו וזו אחות אמו וגופין מוחלקין דג' נשים הוויין:
notes.en: Why do they need these to separate? It is obvious that he is liable for each one by itself, since the names are separate, this one being called his sister, this one his father’s sister and this one his mother’s sister, and the bodies are separate, since they are three women.

messages.text: Rather, say as follows: The verse serves to separate the transgressions and render one liable to bring a separate sin offering for unwittingly engaging in intercourse with his sister who is also his father’s sister and who is also his mother’s sister, i.e., one is liable to bring three sin offerings despite the fact that all three prohibitions are violated through one act of intercourse with the same person.

notes.dh: אחותו שהיא אחות אביו ואחות אמו
notes.he: מפרש לקמן בפ' אמרו לו (כריתות דף טו.) ברשיעא בר רשיעא (כותי) הבא על אמו והוליד שתי בנות ובא על אחת מהן והוליד בן ובא הבן על אחותו שהיא אחות אביו ואחות אמו ועלה איצטריך קרא לחלק משום דגוף אחד הוא:
notes.en: His sister who is his father’s sister and his mother’s sister: this is explained below in the chapter “They Said to Him” (Keritot 15a), with a wicked man son of a wicked man [the Hebrew adds in parentheses: “a Kuti”] who had intercourse with his mother and fathered two daughters, then had intercourse with one of them and fathered a son, and the son had intercourse with his sister [the other daughter], who is his father’s sister and his mother’s sister. For this a verse is needed to separate, since it is one body.

notes.he: תימה דנקט הני דלא משכח אלא באיסור לנקוט אשת אחיו שהיא אשת אחי אביו או בת בתו וכלתו ואחות אשתו כדאמרי' בפ"ג (לקמן יד.) וי"ל דנקט הא לרבותא אע"ג דכל שמות שבה משל אחווה הן אפ"ה חשיבי שמות מחולקין:
notes.en: His sister who is his father’s sister, and so on: it is puzzling that the Gemara chose these, which can come about only through a transgression. Let it choose his brother’s wife who is also his father’s brother’s wife, or his daughter’s daughter who is also his daughter-in-law, and his wife’s sister, as we say in chapter 3 (below, 14a). One can answer that it chose this case for its novelty: although all its names are names of sisterhood, they still count as separate names.

notes.he: אלא אימא מיתבעי להון לחלק על אחותו שהיא אחות אביו ושהיא אחות אמו ומשכחת לה ברשיעא בר רשיעא כגון שבא על אמו והוליד ממנה ב' בנות וחזר ובא על אחת מן הבנות והוליד בן ואותו בן בא על הבת האחרת שהיא אחותו מאביו ואחות אמו ואחות אביו והכא שמות מוחלקין וגוף אחד. מיתבעי להון לחייב על אחותו בת אביו ובת אמו דהא לא אשכחן בקרא אלא בת אביך או בת אמך לומר שאין עונשין מן הדין אע"ג דאתיא מק"ו. השתא בת אביו שלא בת אמו מיחייב בת אביו ובת אמו כ"ש:
notes.en: Rather, say: they need it to separate for his sister who is his father’s sister and who is his mother’s sister. You find it with a wicked man son of a wicked man: for example, one who had intercourse with his mother and fathered two daughters by her, then had intercourse with one of the daughters and fathered a son, and that son had intercourse with the other daughter, who is his sister through his father, his mother’s sister and his father’s sister. Here the names are separate but the body is one. They need it to make him liable for his sister who is both his father’s daughter and his mother’s daughter, since in the verse we find only “your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter” [Leviticus 18:9]. (A printer’s mark notes that the text up to here belongs to the previous page.) [This continues the Gemara on 3a:] to say that one does not punish on the basis of an inference, even though it would follow by a fortiori reasoning: if for his father’s daughter who is not his mother’s daughter he is liable, then for his father’s daughter who is also his mother’s daughter, all the more so.

messages.text: And with regard to Rabbi Yitzḥak, from where does he derive this matter?
messages.lead: The Gemara turns its attention to the other opinion:

messages.text: He derives it from the latter clause of the verse, as it is written: “He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness” (Leviticus 20:17). This seemingly superfluous phrase teaches this halakha.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִקַּח אֶת־אֲחֹתוֹ בַּת־אָבִיו אוֹ בַת־אִמּוֹ וְרָאָה אֶת־עֶרְוָתָהּ וְהִיא־תִרְאֶה אֶת־עֶרְוָתוֹ חֶסֶד הוּא וְנִכְרְתוּ לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי עַמָּם עֶרְוַת אֲחֹתוֹ גִּלָּה עֲוֺנוֹ יִשָּׂא׃
verse.en: If a man marries his sister, the daughter of either his father or his mother, so that he sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace; they shall be excommunicated in the sight of their kinsfolk. He has uncovered the nakedness of his sister, he shall bear the guilt.

messages.text: And with regard to the Rabbis, concerning this mention of “his sister” in the latter clause of the verse, what do they do with it?

notes.he: דקרא דכרת דלעיל נמי עלה קאי:
notes.en: From “his sister” in the latter clause: since the verse of karet above also refers to it.

messages.text: They require it…

notes.he: לא בעי להכי קרא אלא קסבר עונשין מן הדין:
notes.en: [On the Gemara’s continuation on 3a:] And Rabbi Yitzḥak does not need a verse for this, since he holds that one does punish on the basis of an inference.

notes.he: ואי בעית תימא לעיל קא מהדר לר' יוחנן דאמר לכך יצא [כרת באחותו] לחלק אי בעית תימא לחלק יליף עונש מן אזהרה מה אזהרה דהיינו לאו כתיבא אכל ערוה וערוה אף עונש כרת נמי [הוי כמאן דכתיב בכולהו] וליחייב על כל ערוה וערוה:
notes.en: [On the Gemara’s continuation on 3a:] And if you wish, say: above he responds to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said that karet was singled out with his sister to separate. If you wish, say: [as for the rule] to separate, he derives the punishment from the warning: just as the warning, that is, the prohibition, is written for each and every forbidden relation, so too the punishment of karet [is as if written for each of them], and he is liable for each and every forbidden relation.

messages.text: Continued on 3a: “…to teach the halakha in the case of his sister who is both his father’s daughter and his mother’s daughter,” and to say that one does not administer punishment based on an a fortiori inference.
